t: Release Compatibility Checker - public implementations survey
title: Release Compatibility Checker - public implementations survey
definition: Checks compatibility with supported environments and dependencies.
description:
Release Compatibility Checker is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Checks compatibility with supported environments and dependencies. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns Release Compatibility Checker. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves Release Compatibility Checker. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the Release Compatibility Checker capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

The design favors boring reliability over cleverness: well-trodden paths, clear errors, and behavior you can reason about without reading the source. title: Release Compatibility Checker definition of done - practitioner discipline
definition: The definition of done discipline for Release Compatibility Checker: checks compatibility with supported environments and dependencies..
description:
definition of done is the Release Compatibility Checker discipline: Checks compatibility with supported environments and dependencies. It turns Release Compatibility Checker from an event into a repeatable capability.

In practice this means: declare inputs, expected outputs, and acceptance checks before starting; run the smallest meaningful case first and verify it by hand; log every decision with its reason, so the next builder inherits understanding Teams that follow the discipline get predictable builds; teams that skip it get interesting stories. The Signature line prefers predictable builds, and this record's demo makes the discipline concrete and runnable.

t: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Release Compatibi
title: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Release Compatibi
definition: Ladder drill (foundation): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Release Compatibility Checker from a one-paragraph brief.
description:
Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Release Compatibility Checker from a one-paragraph brief

Read the brief twice. List every input the Release Compatibility Checker needs, every output it must produce, and one contract each input-output pair must satisfy. Work it by hand first, then run the demo program and compare its trace against your own reasoning. When they agree, the concept is yours.

Success criterion: you can list them from memory without looking at the brief
